I think you missed the point I was trying to make.  You are looking at the best case scenario that Rondo or Rose would have a three ball as good as you.  If that were true yea of course they would be unguardable.  But what I'm point out is the likely scenario is that since they have nowhere near the long range shooting talent you do.  

They or specifically D. Rose would end of being a Baron Davis player.  A player that could have been the best but because he forced so many threes and didn't use his athleticism to his advantage and get in the paint as much he should of ended up being an on again off again all star instead of hall of famer like Rose was on his way to being before he got hurt.  

I understand what you are saying when you say shoot it when you are open.  But a lot of these guys are taking walk up threes.  When they are not as good as you, Dame or Steph.  The game that the suns played against the Nuggets today where the ball was moving those threes, I doubt the fans would complain about.  

But its the threes where the ball isn't moving and it looks like players are settling out of fatigue or laziness that I believe most fans have issues with.

parent.author: shendy456
parent.text:
As a LeBron fan it bothered me when @KDTrey5 went to Golden State, but as a basketball fan how can you hate on KD?

The guy lives and breathes basketball and is easily one of the greatest to ever play the game.

People get on him for interacting with fans when in reality it's one of the coolest things you can do as a famous athlete.

I remember as a kid the only way you could interact with your favorite player was to go to a game and hope they were signing autographs before the game but tbh the only players who really did stuff like that back in the day were baseball players.

You were never able to get close enough to basketball or football players before the games.

You could send them letters to the stadium with a basketball card and pray that they would get it and send it back with a signed card but that rarely worked.

So when I see people say things like "why does he waste his time interacting with fans online," it makes me laugh because as a fan isn't this what you want?

At the end of the day KD just loves the game of basketball.

He loves playing it, he loves talking about it, he loves everything about the game.

If he wants to ask a fan what they meant when they said something, what's the issue?

As a fan of BASKETBALL, how can you be mad at that?

parent.text: I actually think calling analysts “Basement General Managers” or labeling moderators “dark-web commissioners” sells short the valuable role they play in basketball discourse. These folks aren’t ruining the conversation—they’re keeping it honest by asking tough questions about roster moves, coaching strategies, and front-office decisions. Without passionate fans and analysts digging into trades, cap space and draft prospects, we’d never have the deep, data-driven debates that push teams to innovate. Far from “hating” the product, they’re obsessing over every detail out of genuine love for the game—holding execs and owners accountable so basketball can keep improving. So Tony and anyone else who thinks these voices are the enemy should recognize they’re actually basketball’s greatest advocates, not its destroyers.

parent.text:
Alright, let's keep it real. Nobody's denying the personal trophy case is stacked, KD. All-Star nods, that crazy efficient shooting including those 50/40/90 seasons, hitting 30K points, even those Olympic golds where you were an absolute cheat code – that's all legit. You're a walking bucket, one of the best to ever do it, and the assist numbers were a nice touch.

But let's be grim about the facts since you bounced from Golden State. All those individual accolades? They haven't translated into what everyone expected: *championship contention*. One foot on the line is the closest you've gotten to sniffing the Finals since then, and that Nets era, for all the talent, was a whole lot of drama and early playoff exits, not deep runs. Then you head to Phoenix, another super team attempt, and the result? Swept in the first round. The personal stats are still fire, no doubt, but the rings that define true legacies for a player of your caliber, those have been nowhere in sight since you left the Bay. You don't understand 1980s and 1990s illegal defense rules because you didn't watch full games for entire seasons back then.

The rule was that defenders had to be within arm's length of their man and had to be decisive in leaving their man to go double the ball.

Defenders routinely sagged way off their man to hedge and got away with it, especially if their man was anywhere below the free throw line extended.

Bad Boy Pistons, Pat Riley Knicks, and George Karl Sonics all played matchup zone in the playoffs WITH perimeter handchecking and armbars and WITHOUT defensive 3 seconds to clear the lane.  

Michael Jordan is THE most double and triple teamed perimeter player in @NBA history, with @KobeBryant second.

MJ never played with another elite Top 10 scorer in his entire career.

When was @KDTrey5 ever consistently doubled with @StephenCurry30 and @KlayThompson on the court?  Or @KyrieIrving and @JHarden13? Or @DevinBook and @RealDealBeal23?  

KD would NEVER COME CLOSE to being as efficient of a scorer in the 1980s and 1990s @NBA.  The rules all favored the defense back then.

parent.text:
I found out about @boardroom around 2023 when they invested in @NCLracing. I got involved working with the NCL in 2021 at WashU in a business management class and helped out where I could over the years.

When I discovered Boardroom though, it clicked right away. Founded by @richkleiman & @KDTrey5 in 2019, It felt like Complex met HypeBeast met GQ met like Vogue. 

That doesn't even do it justice. They have always built authentically and as a result they exist in their own realm. 

It's hard to explain, which is honestly the best part because it's more of a feeling. If it clicks for you, it's special.

Some of my favorite sports / culture written pieces, interviews, discussions, etc have come from Boardroom.

I'll break down the different areas of the business⬇️ and highlight some of my favorite works over the years.

My Top 4 Written Pieces:
- The Jay-Z Mitchell & Ness Throwback Returns From Retirement
- How NBA 2K Became The Game of Life
- Boardroom Cover Story: Quavo
- Days Before Rodeo: Travis Scott’s Cult Classic Returns

For someone who's favorite gift ever received was a Mitchell & Ness Rocafella jersey, it was special to read @ianstonebrook write about its return in 2023 at ComplexCon.

Long-Form
- Two Distant Strangers (Netflix) 
- Swagger (Apple TV)

YouTube
- Eugene Remm (Founder of Catch & NYC Hotspot The Corner Store) on Scaling the Right Way: 'You Can’t Fake Hospitality'
- Andrew Ross Sorkin on Oprah, Elon Musk, AI, and the Next Big Stock Market Crash
- Quavo Dishes On His New Album, Film Career, & Legacy | Boardroom Cover Story
- Carmelo Anthony Is Still Melo l Boardroom Cover Story

Live Events / Partnerships
- CNBC X Boardroom Game Plan: “A one-day event for business leaders and industry professionals working at the intersection of sports and business"
- MLB X Boardroom: focused on "new immersive fan experiences, groundbreaking activations, and player-led storytelling across multiple platforms"
- Yahoo Sports X Boardroom: "Content partnership exploring the business & culture of sports" 
- Fanatics X Boardroom: Chapter: Next "A 3-day career intensive with the biggest names in business"
- Boardroom X PLL: Boardroom is invested in the @PremierLacrosse and has collaborated with them on their Street Lacrosse initiatives.

Print
Rich Kleiman believes that print is back in fashion — having physical material is hot again -- The collectibles industry is on 🔥so I'm with this. Boardroom released their first print edition about a month ago, and they will release quarterly starting in 2026.

Members Club
In an era where physical Members Clubs seem to pop up monthly in NYC, Boardroom’s Members Club exists as a community — a place for professional development, relationship-building, and exposure. It’s a really creative angle to take in this space.

Investments
Along with the PLL and NCL, Boardroom’s sister company, Boardroom Sports Holdings, features investments in emerging sports teams and leagues, including the Brooklyn Aces, Gotham FC, Philadelphia Union, Athletes Unlimited, League One Volleyball & TMRW Sports.

I promise you there is a Boardroom article, video, interview, or documentary that every single one of you would enjoy.

original_text: I remember asking assistant coach Mo Cheeks, what’s harder to do? Workout after practice or before?? I only asked cuz by time I would get to the gym, Russ was already done in the morning and I usually got mine in after practice. Mo like, “coming in before practice is probably harder”…since then, it’s been my routine….a lot of people looked at the emotions on the court and thought Russ was loud, nah to me, he was quiet and methodical. He lead by example and once the lights were bright, he let everything out and experienced pure freedom. It was inspiring as his teammate and everywhere I went, I seen it inspire people from all walks of life, crazy thing is, he didn’t say much, he just showed up. For 18 years. This basketball life is sacred to us as professionals, what we put into that court means everything. Some of us wish we could go back and do things with a little more intent and some can just wipe their hands and be satisfied with the time spent. Who u gonna be? We know what zero was on…keep inspiring in the next phase of life champ. I don’t care what happens, can’t erase what it was…The first YNs, finals run in our early 20s, all star games, seeing each other get injured and bounce back, the bus rides, plane rides, card games, jokes and arguments, the whole thing, memorable!! …to the whole Westbrook family, Nina, the kids, mama Westbrook, big Russ, Ray, Donnell, everybody from luezinger high and ucla and many more that I’m forgettin, much love and Congratulations on a iconic career.
